events.title: Battle of Hastings
events.description: Duke William of Normandy defeated King Harold II of England at the Battle of Hastings near the town of Hastings. Harold was killed in the fighting, leaving the English army broken.
events.significance: The Norman victory led to the Norman conquest of England, transforming English language, law, aristocracy, and culture, and reshaping the course of European history.

events.title: Birth of Dwight D. Eisenhower
events.description: Dwight David Eisenhower was born in Denison, Texas. He rose to become Supreme Commander of Allied Expeditionary Forces in Europe during World War II and later served as the 34th President of the United States from 1953 to 1961.
events.significance: Eisenhower oversaw the D-Day invasion of Normandy, and as president he launched the Interstate Highway System, ended the Korean War, and warned of the military-industrial complex.

events.title: Chuck Yeager Breaks the Sound Barrier
events.description: U.S. Air Force Captain Chuck Yeager piloted the rocket-powered Bell X-1 aircraft, nicknamed Glamorous Glennis, over the Mojave Desert, becoming the first person to fly faster than the speed of sound in level flight.
events.significance: The flight proved that supersonic flight was possible and opened the way for modern high-speed aviation and the space age.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: Martin Luther King Jr. was announced as the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize for his nonviolent resistance to racial prejudice in the United States. At age 35, he was the youngest person to have received the award up to that time.
events.significance: The prize brought international recognition to the American civil rights movement and reinforced the moral force of nonviolent protest during the period leading to the Civil Rights Act and the Voting Rights Act.

events.title: Attempted Assassination of Theodore Roosevelt
events.description: While campaigning in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, as the Progressive Party candidate, former President Theodore Roosevelt was shot in the chest by John Schrank. The bullet was slowed by his folded speech and eyeglass case, and Roosevelt went on to deliver his speech before seeking medical care.
events.significance: The incident demonstrated Roosevelt's famed resilience and became a defining moment of the 1912 presidential campaign, which saw the Republican vote split and Woodrow Wilson elected.
